variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

An organisational division in politics is not the same as a change in the rules under which firms operate. Commercial readers should avoid treating the split as a ready-made forecast. Representation and future decisions require examination in their own right, without an assumed programme attached to either part.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
